bc.ch01.kicker: THIS IS PERFORMING FIRE, TRANSMITTING FROM PHASE 1 · 2026 APE LAB, TRACK B (PAIK NAM JUNE)
bc.ch01.title: HOW WILL WE GREET NEW TECHNOLOGY?
bc.ch01.titleSub: 우리는 새로운 기술을 어떻게 맞이할 것인가?
bc.ch01.intro: Performing Fire is an interactive media installation that gathers what artists think and feel about technology — questions, hopes, fears, imaginations — and turns them into a single living fire. Each offering becomes its own flame, with its own shape, motion, and light. Over the exhibition the fire grows: a collective totem of possible futures.
bc.ch01.notes: The future of technology is usually imagined in two directions: possibility and threat. Performing Fire starts somewhere else — from the unstable relationship in which humans change technology and are changed by it in return. Fire was the first technology we never fully tamed; we learned instead to live alongside its instability. Perhaps what we need now is not fear of the new, nor unconditional acceptance, but 불장난 — fire play: an experimental relationship with what can affect us but cannot be fully predicted or controlled.
bc.ch01.step1.name: OFFER 공물
bc.ch01.step1.text: At the installation (or here), tell us your question, hope, or fear about technology. Write it, speak it, or show it.
bc.ch01.step2.name: TRANSFORM 지시문
bc.ch01.step2.text: AI reads each offering — its meaning, temperature, texture — and, in the spirit of Nam June Paik and Fluxus, turns it into a Score: an open proposition anyone can perform in their own way.
bc.ch01.step3.name: BURN 연소
bc.ch01.step3.text: Each offering becomes a flame, projected on translucent fabric, shaped by the words that made it. Different perspectives overlap, collide, and form one collective fire.
bc.ch01.step4.name: PERFORM 수행
bc.ch01.step4.text: In the final weeks, a live performer reinterprets the accumulated voices and Scores with the body — reimagining 달집태우기 (moon-house burning) and 쥐불놀이 (fire play), East Asian rites where communities gathered around fire to wish and to let go.

bc.ch04.kicker: AI reads each offering and, in the spirit of Nam June Paik and Fluxus, returns a Score — an open proposition anyone can perform in their own way. Eight samples on rotation.
bc.ch04.title: SCORES
bc.ch04.score1.title: IGNITION 점화
bc.ch04.score1.text: Write the technology you fear on your palm. Hold it over something warm. Wait until the warmth reaches the word.
bc.ch04.score2.title: MOON HOUSE 달집
bc.ch04.score2.text: Build a small house from things you planned to throw away. Put one wish inside. Do not burn it yet.
bc.ch04.score3.title: FEED 공급
bc.ch04.score3.text: Tell your oldest fear to the youngest machine in your home. Note which of you changes.
bc.ch04.score4.title: ORBIT 쥐불
bc.ch04.score4.text: Swing a light in a circle until it becomes a line. This is how fast a fear must move to look like hope.
bc.ch04.score5.title: ERROR TERM 오차항
bc.ch04.score5.text: Do something one hundred times. Keep only the flicker.
bc.ch04.score6.title: BROADCAST 송출
bc.ch04.score6.text: Hum for thirty seconds to an appliance. If it hums back, you have made a duet. If not, you have made a prayer.
bc.ch04.score7.title: HANDOVER 인계
bc.ch04.score7.text: Let a machine finish your sentence. Finish one of its own. Call it even.
bc.ch04.score8.title: ASH 재
bc.ch04.score8.text: Delete something you made. Describe what remains.
